# Air receiver -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** While the station runs, keep the receiver between the pot less 0.5 bar and the pot: open receiver.supply at the bottom of the band, close it at the top. receiver.pressure is the card's raw count -- 0 at 4 mA, 27648 at 20 mA, over 0..10 bar -- so scale it (NORM_X, then SCALE_X) and show bar on the gauge. Open the isolation valve while the station runs and prove it by valve.opened: it takes 2 s to travel, and if it has not arrived when that and a margin have run out, it has failed -- alarm, and stop.

**Done when.** The needle on the receiver's own gauge and the one you drive agree, and the receiver cycles inside the band -- still after the plant draws harder (the receiver's Consumption) and after you move the pot. Divide by 32767 instead of 27648 and everything reads 16 % low and the receiver runs 16 % high. Seize the valve (valve.fault) and Start: valve.opened never comes, and only a timer on the feedback notices -- but a check without one alarms on every healthy start, because for two seconds neither limit switch is made.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`air_receiver.st`](air_receiver.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Air receiver" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/air_receiver.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   ```bash
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   (From a source checkout: `cd sidecar && python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`.
   If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add `-o host 0.0.0.0` and read the warning
   it prints.) Check the address map it prints against the table below.
3. Compile `air_receiver.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh air_receiver.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 8 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 6 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 4 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 2 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses -- and pass the port it prints:

   ```bash
   python tools/grade.py --scene air-receiver
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alarm.beacon` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `AlarmBeacon` %QX100.0 | rotating alarm beacon | yes |
| `alarm.horn` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `AlarmHorn` %QX100.1 | alarm horn | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.0 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.2 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `PanelRed` %QX100.3 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `PanelReset` %IX100.1 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x0 + 3x1 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW100 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW101 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 4..6.5 bar (starts at 6) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `PanelStart` %IX100.2 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `PanelStop` %IX100.3 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `pressure_gauge.value` | PLC writes | float | 4x0 + 4x1 | `PressureGaugeValueHi` %QW100 + `PressureGaugeValueLo` %QW101 -> `PressureGaugeValue` : REAL | needle position, scale 0..10 bar | yes |
| `receiver.pressure` | PLC reads | int | 3x2 + 3x3 | `ReceiverPressureHi` %IW102 + `ReceiverPressureLo` %IW103 -> `ReceiverPressure` : DINT | receiver pressure, RAW counts: 0 = 0 bar, 27648 = 10 bar, 32767 = wire break | yes |
| `receiver.supply` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `ReceiverSupply` %QX100.4 | open the receiver's supply valve (load the receiver) | yes |
| `receiver.wirebreak` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `ReceiverWirebreak` %IX100.4 | the card's wire-break diagnostic for the 4-20 mA loop | yes |
| `valve.closed` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `ValveClosed` %IX100.5 | limit switch: valve fully closed; mid-travel neither is made (2 s end to end) | yes |
| `valve.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `ValveFault` %IX100.6 | TRUE = the stem has seized; the feedback no longer follows the command | yes |
| `valve.open` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `ValveOpen` %QX100.5 | energise the solenoid: the valve travels open (spring closes it when dropped) | yes |
| `valve.opened` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `ValveOpened` %IX100.7 | limit switch: valve fully open | yes |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 3:
  `panel.setpoint`, `pressure_gauge.value`, `receiver.pressure`. The program's
  first and last sections move them between the registers and plain DINT/REAL
  variables, so your logic never sees a register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL`
  converts the *number* (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the
  starter rebuilds a REAL bit by bit instead.
  [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh) compiles the helpers with
  OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
